title: 571. Discrete Mathematics, Counting & Graph Theory: Solving First-Order Linear Recurrences
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a recurrence in which a constant is added at each step.
questions.question: A sequence satisfies \(a_n=a_{n-1}+3\) with \(a_0=2\). Which formula gives \(a_n\)?
questions.explanation: Each step adds \(3\), so after \(n\) steps the value is \(2+3n\): the sequence is \(2,5,8,11,\dots\) The formula \(2\cdot 3^n\) describes repeated multiplication by \(3\) and gives \(a_1=6\), which is wrong.
questions.hint: Compute the first few terms and look for the pattern.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a recurrence in which each term is a constant multiple of the previous one.
questions.question: A sequence satisfies \(a_n=2a_{n-1}\) with \(a_0=5\). Which formula gives \(a_n\)?
questions.explanation: Each step multiplies by \(2\), so after \(n\) steps the value is \(5\cdot 2^n\): the sequence is \(5,10,20,40,\dots\) The formula \(5+2n\) describes repeated addition of \(2\) and gives \(a_1=7\), which is wrong.
questions.hint: Decide whether the terms grow by a fixed difference or by a fixed factor.

questions.learningObjective: Compute a term of a first-order recurrence by iteration.
questions.question: A sequence satisfies \(a_n=3a_{n-1}-2\) with \(a_0=2\). What is \(a_4\)?
questions.explanation: \(a_1=3\cdot 2-2=4\), \(a_2=3\cdot 4-2=10\), \(a_3=3\cdot 10-2=28\), and \(a_4=3\cdot 28-2=82\). The closed form is \(a_n=3^n+1\), which also gives \(81+1=82\). The number \(80\) results from subtracting once too often.
questions.hint: Apply the rule four times, one term at a time.

questions.learningObjective: Find the closed form of a recurrence that doubles and adds one.
questions.question: A sequence satisfies \(a_n=2a_{n-1}+1\) with \(a_0=0\). Which formula gives \(a_n\)?
questions.explanation: The terms are \(0,1,3,7,15,\dots\), each one less than a power of \(2\). Indeed, if \(a_{n-1}=2^{n-1}-1\), then \(a_n=2(2^{n-1}-1)+1=2^n-1\). The formula \(2^n+1\) gives \(a_0=2\), which contradicts \(a_0=0\).
questions.hint: Compute the first few terms and compare them with powers of \(2\).

questions.learningObjective: Solve a recurrence in which the added amount grows with the index.
questions.question: A sequence satisfies \(a_n=a_{n-1}+n\) with \(a_0=0\). Which formula gives \(a_n\)?
questions.explanation: Unrolling the recurrence gives \(a_n=1+2+\cdots+n=\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}\); the terms are \(0,1,3,6,10,\dots\) The formula \(n^2\) gives \(a_2=4\), but the recurrence gives \(a_2=3\).
questions.hint: Write \(a_n\) as a sum of all the amounts added so far.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a first-order recurrence with multiplier three and a constant term.
questions.question: A sequence satisfies \(a_n=3a_{n-1}+4\) with \(a_0=1\). Which formula gives \(a_n\)?
questions.explanation: Adding \(2\) to both sides gives \(a_n+2=3(a_{n-1}+2)\), so \(a_n+2\) is multiplied by \(3\) at each step: \(a_n+2=3^n(a_0+2)=3^{n+1}\). Hence \(a_n=3^{n+1}-2\); the terms are \(1,7,25,\dots\) The formula \(3^n+4n\) gives \(a_2=17\), but the recurrence gives \(25\).
questions.hint: Look for a constant \(c\) such that \(a_n+c\) is simply multiplied by \(3\) at each step.

questions.learningObjective: Find the constant sequence that satisfies a recurrence.
questions.question: Which constant sequence \(a_n=c\) satisfies \(a_n=\dfrac{1}{2}a_{n-1}+3\)?
questions.explanation: A constant solution must satisfy \(c=\dfrac{1}{2}c+3\), so \(\dfrac{1}{2}c=3\) and \(c=6\). With \(c=3\) the right side would be \(\dfrac{3}{2}+3=\dfrac{9}{2}\), not \(3\).
questions.hint: Replace both \(a_n\) and \(a_{n-1}\) by \(c\) and solve.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a recurrence whose multiplier is the index.
questions.question: A sequence satisfies \(a_n=n\cdot a_{n-1}\) with \(a_0=1\). Which formula gives \(a_n\)?
questions.explanation: Unrolling gives \(a_n=n\cdot(n-1)\cdots 2\cdot 1\cdot a_0=n!\); the terms are \(1,1,2,6,24,\dots\) The formula \(2^n\) gives \(a_3=8\), but the recurrence gives \(a_3=6\).
questions.hint: The multiplier changes from step to step.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a first-order recurrence with a negative constant term.
questions.question: A sequence satisfies \(a_n=2a_{n-1}-3\) with \(a_0=5\). Which formula gives \(a_n\)?
questions.explanation: Subtracting \(3\) from both sides gives \(a_n-3=2(a_{n-1}-3)\), so \(a_n-3=2^n(a_0-3)=2^{n+1}\) and \(a_n=2^{n+1}+3\). The terms are \(5,7,11,19,\dots\) The formula \(5\cdot 2^n-3\) gives \(a_0=2\), which contradicts \(a_0=5\).
questions.hint: Find the constant solution first, then study the difference between \(a_n\) and that constant.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a recurrence by summing the added terms.
questions.question: A sequence satisfies \(a_n=a_{n-1}+2n-1\) with \(a_0=0\). Which formula gives \(a_n\)?
questions.explanation: Unrolling gives \(a_n=1+3+5+\cdots+(2n-1)\), the sum of the first \(n\) odd numbers, which is \(n^2\). The terms are \(0,1,4,9,\dots\) The formula \(n^2+n\) gives \(a_1=2\), but the recurrence gives \(a_1=1\).
questions.hint: Compute the first few terms and recognise them.
